title: Ticket #166 Phase 2 Planning Sideshow Dogfood
objective: Dogfood ticket #166 Phase 2 by keeping a real implementation plan in canonical structured data, projecting it into authored slides, and proving the example is repeatable without trusting review annotations as source data.

outcomes.description: A strict schema-version-2 planning contract exists for the real ticket #166 Phase 2 scope and every canonical identifier is projected into the deck.
proof: examples/planning-sideshow/plan.json uses schema_version 2 and task verification.intent plus verification.commands
cargo run -- plan check examples/planning-sideshow --strict covers every plan ID through stable data-plan-kind and data-plan-id anchors

outcomes.description: Slides demonstrate the Phase 2 planning visual grammar with authored rails, layers, connectors, and native evidence disclosures rather than a synthetic wall of cards.
proof: the narrative separates sequence, trust boundary, dependencies, and proof evidence

outcomes.description: The repository contains a repeatable example with local edit, strict check, build, review, and export commands documented for future agents and humans.
proof: examples/planning-sideshow/README.md documents the repeatable loop and output locations
root README.md points to the example and shows validation/build commands

outcomes.description: Documentation and dogfood content define Markdown as a derived manual drafting digest of per-task packets, while JSON remains the normalized strict schema-v2 machine boundary.
proof: docs/PLANNING.md and README.md describe the digest as source material rather than tracker issues
examples/planning-sideshow/slides/05-manual-digest.html shows rationale to packets to manual tracker translation

constraints.description: Keep Sideshow focused on alignment, review, tracker-neutral digest building blocks, and expressive authoring; do not add tracker integrations, imported tracker state, execution synchronization, or committed dist output.
Review annotations are feedback only; canonical edits happen in plan.json and slides, and executable commands come only from trusted structured plan data or documented repository commands.
Every verification and build command must be runnable from the repository root with cargo run -- ... or nix develop -c cargo run -- ... variants.

Markdown digest packets are trusted drafting material but are not guaranteed 1:1 issues; humans or agents choose split/combine boundaries, labels, teams, priority, milestones, and tracker conventions.

non_goals: Do not create review UI changes or alter the review trust model implementation.
Do not make Sideshow create tracker issues, ingest tracker state, or manage execution after handoff.
Do not commit generated dist HTML or temporary JSON/Markdown exports.
Do not use this example as a synthetic fixture detached from ticket #166 Phase 2.

decisions.title: Use ticket #166 Phase 2 as the dogfood subject
decisions.rationale: A real repository planning deck exercises the contract, documentation, and reviewer handoff better than a made-up fixture.

decisions.title: Keep slides authored and anchored
decisions.rationale: The deck should persuade humans with expressive projections while strict checks ensure every canonical plan ID remains visible.

decisions.title: Leave generated output outside the change
decisions.rationale: Repeatability is proven by commands and inspected output, but the repository example stays source-only.

decisions.title: Treat Markdown as a derived manual drafting digest
decisions.rationale: Strict normalized JSON is the machine contract. Markdown can group task packets for readability and prompt handoff, but tracker boundaries remain a human or agent translation decision.

tasks.title: Model the Phase 2 work as strict canonical plan data

outcomes, dependencies, files, acceptance checks, decisions, constraints, risks, and exact repository commands describe the real ticket #166 Phase 2 work

verification.intent: Confirm the canonical plan is parseable, internally linked, and fully projected before the example is treated as reviewable.

tasks.title: Author expressive anchored slides

slides include plan rail, layers, connectors, and native plan evidence disclosure without review UI changes

verification.intent: Prove the authored projection remains complete after visual composition changes.

tasks.title: Document the repeatable local workflow
acceptance_checks: documentation describes an alignment-first lifecycle that ends with a human- or agent-authored tracker digest rather than synchronized execution
documentation presents later demos and project summaries as separate authoring workflows assembled from available context without built-in ingestion

cargo run -- plan export examples/planning-sideshow --format markdown --output "$export_dir/plan.md"

tasks.title: Dogfood the tracker-neutral planning digest increment
acceptance_checks: README, planning docs, example docs, and authoring skill guidance describe the tracker-neutral digest contract without adding tracker APIs or execution history

every new canonical ID has a data-plan-kind/data-plan-id slide anchor and strict projection coverage remains complete
each packet repeats the objective, names a stable canonical workstream/task path, points to shared plan context, and preserves exact commands in individually fenced shell blocks

verification.intent: Confirm the documentation/dogfood digest increment preserves strict projection coverage and builds without committing generated output.

risks.description: Slides could become persuasive but incomplete if authored anchors drift away from canonical plan IDs.
risks.mitigation: Run cargo run -- plan check examples/planning-sideshow --strict after every content edit and keep IDs stable.

risks.description: Readers could mistake review annotations or local UI state for canonical plan updates.
risks.mitigation: State the trust boundary in the deck and README: annotations are feedback only; plan.json and slides are the source of truth.

risks.description: Generated dist or export files could accidentally enter the repository change and obscure the source-only example.
risks.mitigation: Build for validation, inspect output exists, remove examples/planning-sideshow/dist before handoff, and keep exports in a fresh directory created with mktemp -d.
